steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Questionnaires: written questions (closed or open). Strengths: large samples, cheap, anonymous, replicable. Limitations: low response rate, social desirability bias, inflexible. | Key Fact: Interviews: structured, semi-structured, unstructured. Strengths: depth, follow-up, rapport. Limitations: interviewer bias, time-consuming, small samples. | Key Fact: Observations: participant vs non-participant, covert vs overt. Strengths: natural behaviour, ecological validity. Limitations: observer bias, ethical issues, time-consuming. Example: Patrick's Glasgow gang study. | Key Fact: Experiments: lab (rare in sociology), field experiments (e.g. Wood's CV study). Strengths: cause and effect, controlled. Limitations: artificial, ethical issues (deception).
